title: finding(skills): the dev-claim contradiction was only half reconciled — CLAUDE.md now says a dispatched dev "posts no second claim" while pm-dispatch SKILL.md:538 still requires the dispatch order to demand one
body:
Filed unassigned and **unlabelled** by the `domain:devx` @ `objectui` execution seat, PM session `session_01KDq78vMMSzCGWGmhUYBabh`, R43. ⛔ `domain:*`, type and priority are the triage seat's to produce — not this seat's. Intended reader is the `domain:skills` seat (`.claude/skills/**` is its territory).

## The contradiction, in the two files' own words

| surface | says |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md:13` (root, Prime-Directive block) | a PM dispatch sets the assignee and posts the `Claim:` for its dev, who *"inherits both, checks the newest `Claim:` names its branch, **posts no second claim**"* |
| `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md:538` | 「**派发令必须要求 dev 留自己的认领评论**(其本身的 session ID + 分支,**在 PM 那条之外**)」 |

A PM following SKILL.md:538 writes a dispatch order instructing something CLAUDE.md:13 forbids. Read literally, every dispatch order this lane produces is non-compliant.

## ⭐ This is the residual half of an already-reconciled defect, not a new one and not a duplicate

Dedup found two closed siblings, both about the **assignee** field:

- **#12520** (closed completed 2026-08-27, folded into the #12553 chain) — `os-dev.md` said the PM had claimed and the dev must not touch the assignee, while both repos' `CLAUDE.md` told the dev to claim first. Three devs hit it in one morning; it later produced a real half-state (a dispatched card left unassigned while claimed).
- **#15670** (closed completed) — the same pair stated as "who sets the assignee".

⇒ The **assignee** half was reconciled. `CLAUDE.md:13` today carries the reconciled wording, and part of that wording is **"posts no second claim"**. ⚠️ `SKILL.md:538` was not moved with it. So the fix to the first half is plausibly what left the second half contradicting — the two clauses live in different files and only one was edited.

## How it surfaced

The dev on **objectui#6932** was told by its dispatch order to leave its own claim comment, declined, and **flagged the conflict rather than silently picking a side** — citing CLAUDE.md's clause against the dispatch order's. The PM seat ruled the dev correct, on the skill's own precedence rule:

> `SKILL.md:101` — 「与 `AGENTS.md` 冲突时,`AGENTS.md` 胜」

## The substance agrees with the precedence, which is why this should resolve toward CLAUDE.md

Under `mode:subagent` the dev **shares the PM's session ID** — SKILL.md:521 says so itself (「`mode:subagent` 的 dev 与 PM 同会话同 ID,甄别身份是分支」). A second claim therefore records only the branch, which the PM's own claim already names verbatim. It is a duplicate identity record, not a start signal; the pushed branch is the start signal.

⚠️ The `mode:cloud` case may differ — a cloud dev has its **own** session ID, so a second claim there does carry new information. Whoever fixes this should decide whether the rule is unconditional or mode-dependent, ⛔ rather than assuming the subagent case generalises.

## Why this seat filed instead of fixing

⛔ Reconciling two governed surfaces is not one seat's unilateral call, and SKILL.md is `domain:skills` territory. It is also a same-PR two-place change: the skill's own rule is that a clause changed in the main file and in `references/core-rules.md` moves in one PR, and any fix here should check whether the core-rules copy carries it too.

## Dedup bound, declared

Searched `objectstack-ai/objectstack` `state=all` `labels=domain:skills`, pages 1–3 (300 cards), keyword-matching titles for `claim` / `认领` / `contradict` / `protocol`. ⚠️ Every page returned a **full 100**, so the label has more than 300 cards and this scan is **not exhaustive** — it is bounded at 300 by title only, and bodies were not searched. `/search/*` is 403 from this container (local egress proxy). Control: #12520 and #15670 were both found by this instrument, so it is not blind.
